title: Additive-functor vanishing on finitely generated integer modules from cyclic summands
statement: Let $R=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z)$, and let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive category: its morphism sets are abelian groups and composition is bilinear. Let $F:\operatorname{Mod}_R\to\mathcal C$ be additive, meaning it preserves sums of morphisms. Let $M$ be an $R$-module whose underlying additive group is generated by finitely many elements. Let $d\in\mathbf N$ and suppose $d x=0$ for every $x\in M$. If $F(\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z/e))$ is a zero object for every natural $e$ dividing $d$, then $F(M)$ is a zero object. All lifted groups have their canonical integer scalar action. A zero object means an object both initial and terminal. We include $\mathbf Z/0=\mathbf Z$ and $0\mid0$.

source.place: AddCommGroup.equiv_free_prod_directSum_zmod, lines 119-132, plus the cyclic-decomposition step in the original item docstring and Stacks Tag 0F08 proof.

proof.text: Apply the structure theorem to M, then lift its finite free-times-cyclic decomposition to the module universe. Its additive equivalence is lifted-integer linear: each lifted integer is the cast of its down-value and additive maps commute with integer scalar multiplication.

Transport the annihilator equation to the decomposition. For every free index, evaluate d on its single generator of value 1; the resulting integer equation forces d=0, so H(0) applies. For every torsion index, evaluate d on its single generator of value 1; ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff gives that its order divides d, so H applies.

Write the identity of the lifted decomposition as the sum of projection followed by inclusion over all free indices and all torsion indices. Check this equality on each coordinate, using finite sums of single functions. Applying F maps this sum to the sum of the composites of its mapped arrows. Each composite factors through a zero object by the preceding step, and hence is zero. Thus the identity on the image is zero. Transport zero-ness to F(M) along the mapped linear equivalence.

theorem isZero_obj_of_fg_of_cyclic
    {C : Type v} [Category.{w} C] [Preadditive C]
    (F : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) ⥤ C) [F.Additive]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)) [AddGroup.FG M]
    (d : ℕ) (hM : ∀ x : M, d • x = 0)
    (H : ∀ e : ℕ, e ∣ d →
      IsZero (F.obj (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ) (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod e))))) :
    IsZero (F.obj M)
